alt: Production paused after the 2023 model year; a redesigned Bolt returned later.

issues.t: High-voltage battery fire risk
issues.sym: Usually no warning beforehand; in rare cases smoke or fire from under the car, often while charging or after charging to full.
issues.why: Some battery cells had manufacturing defects that could cause an internal short. GM recalled every Bolt EV of these years and replaced battery modules or packs.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and leave the hood closed. Call 911 from a safe spot, even if you can't see flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Check the VIN for open recalls right away. Until the remedy is done, follow GM's charging limits and park outside, away from buildings.

issues.t: Battery monitoring software not installed correctly
issues.sym: Usually nothing you notice, which is why the VIN check matters.
issues.why: Diagnostic software added during the battery recall was not installed correctly on some cars, so a faulty battery module could go undetected. GM issued follow-up recalls to reinstall it.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls and have a Chevrolet EV dealer confirm the latest battery software is installed. Park outside until it is.

issues.t: Sudden loss of power with charge still showing
issues.sym: The range estimate drops quickly or the car loses drive power while the gauge still shows charge left, sometimes with a propulsion power reduced message.
issues.why: The battery software could miss a weak group of cells dropping to low voltage, so it overestimated range and gave little warning before shutting down propulsion. GM released a software update, and some cars got new battery packs.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Make sure GM bulletin 18125 (N172127150) and all later battery updates are done. If range suddenly falls, keep the charge higher and have the battery checked.

issues.t: Seat belt pretensioner can ignite carpet after a crash
issues.sym: Nothing before a crash. After a crash that fires the front seat belt pretensioners, smoke or flames could come from the carpet near the door pillar.
issues.why: Hot gas from the pretensioner could ignite nearby carpet. GM recalled affected cars to add foil shielding, then recalled some again because the first repair was not done correctly.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls. After any crash, get everyone out and watch for smoke near the front seats.

issues.t: Rear brake calipers may lose braking force
issues.sym: Weaker braking or a brake pedal that travels farther than normal.
issues.why: A coating on the rear caliper pistons may be insufficient, letting gas pockets form that reduce rear braking. GM recalled affected cars.
issues.next: If the brake pedal sinks, feels soft or goes closer to the floor, or a red brake warning comes on, slow down gently, use a lower gear, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on: call for a tow. Check the VIN for an open recall and have the calipers replaced. Get the brakes checked before driving if the pedal feels different.

issues.t: Front left brake caliper may crack
issues.sym: Usually no warning before it breaks; a cracked caliper can cause a soft pedal, a pull to one side, or leaking brake fluid.
issues.why: Some front left calipers were cast improperly and could fracture under high braking pressure. GM recalled affected cars.
issues.next: If the brake pedal sinks, feels soft or goes closer to the floor, or a red brake warning comes on, slow down gently, use a lower gear, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on: call for a tow. Check the VIN for an open recall. If braking feels weak or you see fluid, do not drive until it is inspected.

issues.t: Rear door may open unexpectedly
issues.sym: The rear inside door handle may stop working, or a rear door could open when you do not expect it.
issues.why: The rear inside door-handle cable may be too long. GM recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check the VIN for an open recall and keep children away from rear doors that behave oddly until the repair is done.

issues.t: Seat belt may not be properly anchored
issues.sym: Usually nothing you notice; a belt anchor could feel loose.
issues.why: The wrong bolts may have been used to attach some seat belts. GM recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check the VIN for an open recall and have the anchors inspected and corrected.

issues.t: Driver airbag may not be secured
issues.sym: Often nothing you can see; an airbag warning light may appear in some cases.
issues.why: A fastener holding the driver airbag to the steering wheel could be missing or loose from the factory. GM recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls and have the dealer inspect and tighten the fasteners.

issues.t: Passenger airbag may not deploy correctly
issues.sym: Nothing you can see in normal driving.
issues.why: Some instrument panels were missing a tear seam needed for the passenger airbag to deploy properly. GM recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check the VIN for an open recall and have the instrument panel repaired.

issues.t: 12-volt battery dies and car will not turn on
issues.sym: The key fob may not unlock the doors, the screens stay dark or the car will not go into Ready, even though the big drive battery is charged. Warning messages may appear after a jump.
issues.why: Like a gas car, the Bolt runs its computers, locks and the main battery switch from a small 12-volt battery. When that battery gets old or weak, the car cannot wake up the high-voltage system. GM asked dealers for information on these no-start cases.
issues.next: Jump the 12-volt battery from another car or a jump pack (the terminals are under the hood), then have the 12-volt battery tested and replaced if it fails. Do not try to jump anything from the orange high-voltage parts.

issues.t: A/C stops blowing cold
issues.sym: The air conditioning blows warm or only slightly cool air, may stop working entirely, or a refrigerant-related service message appears.
issues.why: Owners report refrigerant leaks from A/C lines and from the electric A/C compressor, a failed compressor, and pressure sensor faults that let the system ice up. The Bolt uses the same A/C system to cool the drive battery, so this matters more than in a gas car.
issues.next: Have the A/C checked for leaks with a dye or electronic detector before paying for a recharge. Ask whether the compressor is covered by the 8-year/100,000-mile EV component warranty on your car.

issues.t: Car will not charge from a home or public charger
issues.sym: The car shows a charging error or simply will not charge on a Level 1 or Level 2 charger, even though the charger and outlet work for other cars.
issues.why: The onboard charger module, which converts household AC power into DC for the drive battery, can fail. GM put this part under a quality watch for 2017-2018 cars, and owners have had it replaced.
issues.next: First rule out the cord and outlet by trying another charger. If the car still will not charge, have a Chevrolet EV dealer scan it. The onboard charger is normally covered by the 8-year/100,000-mile EV component warranty.

issues.t: Loss of drive power from a failed battery disconnect relay
issues.sym: The car suddenly loses drive power or shuts down with charge still showing, then will not drive or charge until it is towed and repaired.
issues.why: The relay or fuse inside the high-voltage battery that connects it to the rest of the car can fail. Owners report replaced battery disconnect relays and main battery fuses. This is separate from the battery recall.
issues.next: Pull over safely and turn on your hazards if power drops. Have the car towed to a Chevrolet EV dealer; these parts are normally covered by the 8-year/100,000-mile EV component warranty.

issues.t: Creak or clunk from the rear axle
issues.sym: A creaking, clunking or pinging sound from the back of the car, mostly at low speed over bumps, uneven pavement or driveways.
issues.why: Owners trace this to the rear axle (twist beam) assembly or one of its bushings. Dealers have replaced the whole rear axle in many cases.
issues.next: Have the rear suspension inspected while the noise is fresh, and note when it happens. If the car is still under warranty, ask the dealer to check the rear axle assembly.

issues.t: Clicking or clunking from front stabilizer links
issues.sym: A metallic click, tink or clunk from the front when going over bumps or turning at low speed, often worse in warm weather.
issues.why: The small ball joints at the ends of the front stabilizer (sway bar) links wear or dry out. GM Korea issued a notice for this noise on Korean-market Bolts built from late 2016 to mid-2018.
issues.next: Not urgent, but have the links checked. Replacing them is a quick job; make sure the left and right parts are the correct ones.

issues.t: Squeak from steering when turning
issues.sym: A squeak from the steering when you turn the wheel in either direction, usually at low speed or when parking.
issues.why: The steering gear shaft can rub against a plastic cap on top of the steering gear. GM bulletin 21-NA-213 covers it on 2017-2022 Bolt EV and 2022 Bolt EUV.
issues.next: Ask a Chevrolet dealer to check for bulletin 21-NA-213. The fix is cleaning and greasing the contact point, not replacing the steering gear.

issues.t: Touchscreen freezes or loses settings
issues.sym: The center screen freezes, stops responding to touches, reboots, loses saved settings, or the camera icon is grayed out.
issues.why: Early radio and display software had bugs. GM released radio reprogramming (bulletin 17NA071) and, in some cases, replaced the display control module (18NA138).
issues.next: Make sure all software updates have been done at a Chevrolet dealer. If the screen keeps freezing after updates, ask about the display module bulletin.

issues.t: Rusted brake rotors from light brake use
issues.sym: Grinding or scraping when braking, a rough pedal feel, or visible rust rings on the brake discs, often at low mileage.
issues.why: Regenerative braking does most of the stopping, so the friction brakes are used so little that rust builds up on the rotors and pads instead of being wiped off.
issues.next: Use the brakes firmly now and then in a safe place to clean the rotors. If grinding continues, have the brakes inspected; badly rusted rotors and pads need replacing.

issues.t: Portable charge cord shows a fault or will not charge
issues.sym: The portable charge cord that came with the car shows a red or flashing fault light, or the car says it is not charging when plugged into the cord.
issues.why: The supplied cord sets have their own electronics that can fail. GM issued bulletins about 120V cords that do not work (17NA341) and on warranty replacement of the newer dual-level cord (22-NA-083). A loose or overheated wall outlet can cause the same symptom.
issues.next: Stop using a cord or outlet that feels hot, smells burnt or looks melted. Try a different outlet or charger, then ask a dealer to test the cord; it is covered under the bumper-to-bumper warranty.

issues.t: Portable charge cord may not cut power if ground is lost (recall)
issues.sym: Usually nothing you notice while charging.
issues.why: Some Webasto portable charge cords supplied with the Bolt EUV had incorrect software and might keep charging if the ground connection was lost, which could expose someone to a brief electric shock. GM recalled the cords.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls and bring the cord to a Chevrolet dealer; they will check its serial number and replace it for free if it is affected.

issues.t: Hum or drone from the front at highway speed
issues.sym: A vibration, hum or drone from the front of a Bolt EUV at about 40-60 mph.
issues.why: A gap between the front bumper beam and an air baffle behind the grille lets the baffle vibrate. GM bulletin 22-NA-024 adds foam tape to stop it.
issues.next: Ask a Chevrolet dealer to check for bulletin 22-NA-024. It is not a safety problem.
